description: Stream-triggered tasks - CREATE TASK ... WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA('s') AS ... - the canonical incremental-processing pattern: the body runs only when the named stream has unconsumed data, EXECUTE TASK triggers a run deterministically, the WHEN condition is re-evaluated on every execution, and a body that reads the stream itself loads the changed rows. Converted 1:1 from features/StreamTriggeredTaskTest (now retired). The three tests that assert the body's rows immediately skip the snowflake backend, as the Java class did: live EXECUTE TASK is asynchronous, so the body's side effects land after the statement returns.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE STREAM src_stream ON TABLE src
CREATE TABLE tgt (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TASK load_tgt WAREHOUSE = 'compute_wh' WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA('src_stream') AS INSERT INTO tgt SELECT id, name FROM src
EXECUTE TASK load_tgt
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tgt

skip.reason: live EXECUTE TASK runs asynchronously; immediate row counts are embedded-only
